questions.question: Users occasionally delete blobs by mistake. You must be able to recover deleted blobs for 14 days. What should you enable?

options.text: Blob soft delete with a retention period of 14 days
options.why: Correct. Soft-deleted blobs can be undeleted during the retention period.

options.text: Container soft delete with a retention period of 14 days
options.why: Container soft delete recovers deleted containers, not individual blobs.

options.text: A CanNotDelete resource lock on the storage account
options.why: Resource locks protect the account resource, not blob data.
Replication copies deletes to the secondary region.

questions.explanation: Blob soft delete retention can be set from 1 to 365 days.

questions.question: A document blob is overwritten with incorrect content. You must be able to restore the previous content automatically for future overwrites without taking manual copies. What should you enable?

options.why: Correct. Each write keeps the previous content as a version.
Snapshots must be taken manually or by a scheduled process.
The change feed logs changes but does not keep previous content.
Access tracking records reads and is used by lifecycle rules.

questions.explanation: Restore a previous version by copying it over the current blob or making it the current version.

questions.question: A container named reports was deleted. Container soft delete is enabled. Which Azure CLI command restores the container?

options.why: Correct. The deleted version is listed by az storage container list --include-deleted.
This restores soft-deleted blobs in an existing container.
This restores a deleted file share.
Failover changes the primary region.

questions.explanation: Container soft delete keeps the container and its blobs during the retention period.

questions.question: You need to configure point-in-time restore for block blobs in a storage account. Which three features must be enabled? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.why: Correct. Point-in-time restore depends on versions.
Correct. The change feed tracks the changes to undo.
Correct. The restore window must be shorter than the soft delete retention.
Object replication is not required for point-in-time restore.

questions.explanation: Point-in-time restore needs versioning, the change feed and blob soft delete.

questions.question: Blob soft delete and container soft delete are enabled on a storage account. You must also prevent an administrator from accidentally deleting the storage account itself. What should you configure?

options.text: A CanNotDelete resource lock on the storage account
options.why: Correct. Soft delete does not protect against deletion of the account.
Versioning protects blob content, not the account resource.

options.text: A longer soft delete retention period
options.why: Retention applies to blobs and containers only.
Stored access policies apply to SAS tokens.

questions.explanation: Use a resource lock to protect the storage account resource from deletion.
